transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came because… I can’t keep my words in a straight line anymore. Like I’ll start trying to explain something from an overnight shift, and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts, and people just kind of stare at me like they’re lost. I can see it happening, but I can’t seem to stop the jumping around.
Have you been experiencing any unusual thoughts or perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don’t?

Not really like… voices, I don’t think. It’s more that I know something is going on at work. The supervisors keep changing my shifts, and everyone says, “Oh, it’s just staffing shortages,” but that doesn’t feel right. It’s like they’re watching me through the unit cameras, checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up.

And I mean, cameras are there anyway, right? Like in the halls, near the nurses’ station, all that. So people act like I’m making a big leap, but I’m not. The schedule changes, the way they look at me after, it all connects. I try to explain it and then they just say I’m stressed, but I’m pretty sure they’re monitoring me.
Do you feel that certain events, actions, or even things people say are specifically directed at you or have a special meaning for you that others don’t seem to notice?

Yeah… yeah, that’s kind of what I mean. Like with the shift changes, it’s not just random. People keep saying it’s staffing shortages, but I’m sure the supervisors changed my shifts on purpose, like they’re testing me or watching if I’m unsafe.

And the cameras on the unit… everyone acts like, “Well, of course there are cameras,” but it’s the way they look at me after, you know? Like something happened on the footage, or they’re checking me. I’ll be trying to explain that, and then I think about how the night shift used to be easier because the halls were quieter, except then they changed that too, and it all kind of points back to me.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being taken out of your head or broadcasted to others?

I don’t know about thoughts being put in or taken out exactly… it’s not like I can point to that. It’s more like they already know things, like the supervisors are watching me through the unit cameras and then changing my shifts after, like they’re checking if I’m unsafe.

People keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, but that doesn’t line up to me. Because the cameras are there, and then someone looks at me a certain way, and then my schedule gets moved, and then I’m on a different floor or different hours, and… sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked. But it feels connected. Like they’re monitoring me.

Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being placed in your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being removed from your mind, or even that your thoughts are being heard by others around you?

I don’t think it’s like… somebody putting thoughts in there, no. Or taking them out. I don’t really know what that would feel like.

The heard-by-others thing… I mean, sometimes I wonder if people know what I’m thinking, but then I don’t know if that’s just because I’m acting different and they can tell. Like if I’m quiet on the unit, people notice, and then they start looking at me, and then I start thinking about what I was doing before that, and it kind of… I lose the thread.

So I guess, no, not exactly like my thoughts are being broadcast. I’m not sure.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being placed in your mind by someone else, or like they're being taken out of your head, or that other people can hear your thoughts?

Not really like someone is putting thoughts in my head or taking them out. I keep saying that part isn’t… it’s not exactly it.

It’s more that I know they’re watching me. Like the supervisors, through the unit cameras, and then my shifts get changed after. People keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, like that explains everything, but it doesn’t. They move me around and watch how I act, like they’re trying to see if I’m unsafe or something.

And then if I try to explain that, it sounds like I’m not answering right, but that’s the thing I mean. It’s not my thoughts being pulled out, it’s them already checking on me and changing things because of me.
Do you ever feel like things that are happening around you, like things people say or do, or events in general, are directly related to you in a special way that others don’t seem to notice?

Yeah… yeah, that’s more like what I mean. Like, at work, when the supervisors move my shifts around, it’s not random to me. They say it’s staffing shortages, everybody keeps saying that, but it feels too lined up with what I’m doing.

Like the cameras on the unit are there, and then I’ll notice someone watching me, or acting different, and then suddenly my schedule changes or I’m put somewhere else. It feels like they’re checking if I’m unsafe. Other people don’t seem to see that connection, but I do.

And I know it sounds like I’m making a big thing out of scheduling, but it’s not just scheduling. It’s the way it happens after they’ve been watching.
Do you ever feel like random things people do or say—like something on TV, a song playing, or even strangers talking—are sending you secret messages meant just for you?

Not like songs or TV so much… I don’t really watch TV the same way lately anyway, it’s usually just on in the room and people are talking over it.

It’s more at work. Like I said, the supervisors… they watch through the unit cameras, and then my shifts get moved around. People keep saying, “Oh, it’s staffing,” but it’s not just that. It happens after they’ve been watching me, like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to do something wrong.

So I don’t know if that counts as secret messages. It’s not a song telling me something. It’s more like the things they do are about me, and everybody acts like I’m not supposed to notice.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being controlled by something outside of yourself, like someone or something is influencing them?

I don’t know if controlled is the right word. Not like a remote control or something. It’s more like… when I’m at work, I start thinking about how I’m acting because I know they’re watching through the unit cameras.

And then the supervisors change my shifts, and everybody says, “It’s just staffing shortages,” but it doesn’t feel like just staffing. It’s always after they’ve been watching me, like they’re trying to see if I’m unsafe.

So maybe that influences my thoughts, yeah, because I can’t stop thinking about what they’re seeing or what they’re going to do with it. But I wouldn’t say they’re putting thoughts in there. It’s just… they’re watching, and then things change because of me.

Do you ever feel like the thoughts you’re having are being placed in your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being heard or known by other people around you without you saying them out loud?

I don’t think they’re, like, putting thoughts in my head exactly. Or hearing them word-for-word. It’s more… they already know what they’re looking for with me.

Like at work, with the cameras on the unit, I’m sure the supervisors are watching me to see if I’m unsafe. Then my shifts get changed, and everyone keeps saying it’s staffing shortages, but that doesn’t make sense to me because it happens after they’ve been watching. So maybe they don’t hear my thoughts, but they know enough. They act like they know what I’m going to do before I do it.

And then I start thinking about it more, and I probably look nervous, and then that probably just makes them watch more. It’s hard to explain.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being placed in your mind by someone else, or like they're being removed from your mind, or that other people can hear your thoughts?

I mean… not exactly like somebody is taking my thoughts out or putting them in, no. I don’t know how that would even feel.

But people act like they already know something about me. Like at work, the supervisors watch through the unit cameras, and then suddenly my shifts get changed. Everybody keeps saying it’s just staffing shortages, like I’m supposed to just accept that, but it keeps happening after they’ve been watching me. So it feels like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up.

It’s not that they can hear every thought in my head. It’s more like they know enough from watching, and then they do things because of it. And then I start thinking about that all day, even when I’m trying to just do my job.

Do you feel that certain actions or events that don’t seem to involve you are actually about you, like people are talking about you when you’re not around or making decisions based on something you did, even if others don’t see that connection?

Yeah… yeah, that happens. Like with my shifts at work. People act like it’s just scheduling or staffing shortages, but I don’t buy that.

They’ve got the unit cameras, and I’m sure the supervisors are watching me on them, checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to do something wrong. Then after that, my shifts get changed. And everybody says, “No, it’s not about you,” but it feels very clearly about me.

I mean, I’ll be trying to just do my rounds or whatever, and then I notice little things, like who’s standing at the desk, who goes quiet when I walk by—well, I guess that’s not really the question. But the shift thing, yeah. That doesn’t feel random. It feels like a decision they make because of me.
Do you ever feel like things that happen around you — like people’s actions, TV shows, or random events — are secretly about you or meant to send you a message?

Yeah… not like TV shows or, I don’t know, billboards or something. I don’t really mean it like that.

It’s more at work. Like the cameras on the unit — I’m sure the supervisors watch me through them, and then my shifts get changed. People keep saying it’s just staffing shortages, but it always feels like it happens after they’ve been watching me, like they’re trying to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up.

And then everyone acts normal, like I’m supposed to not notice. I used to try to ignore it and just do my job, but once you see the pattern it’s hard to unsee it. Like even if they don’t say it directly, it feels like the whole thing is about me.
Do you ever feel like something outside of yourself is directly controlling your actions or thoughts, like someone or something is making you think or act in ways you don’t want to?

Not like… someone is moving my arms or making words come out of my mouth. I don’t think it’s like that.

But at work, it kind of feels like they’re controlling what happens to me, if that makes sense. Like the supervisors watch me through the unit cameras, and then my shifts get changed. Everybody keeps saying it’s just staffing shortages, but that’s too easy. It’s always after they’ve been watching, like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up.

And then I start changing how I act because of it, like trying not to look nervous, trying to be careful where I stand, and then it makes me look worse probably. I don’t know. So not controlling my thoughts exactly, but they get in my head, because I know they’re watching.

Do you feel that certain everyday events or actions by others — things that might seem normal or random to most people — are actually directly connected to you or have a special meaning for you that others don’t seem to notice?

Yeah… I mean, mostly at work. Like people will say, “Oh, it’s just staffing,” or “Your shift got moved because someone called out,” but it doesn’t feel random to me.

It feels connected to me because the supervisors have the unit cameras, and I’m sure they’re watching me through them, like checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up. And then suddenly my shifts change. That’s not just nothing.

I know other people don’t see it that way. They act like I’m reading too much into it, but… I don’t know, when it keeps happening like that, it feels like it means something. Like they made that decision because of me.
Do you ever feel like things people do or say—like something on TV, a song playing, or even strangers talking—are sending you secret messages meant just for you?

Not TV or songs, not really. I mean, sometimes people bring up stuff like that and it sounds… I don’t know, too dramatic.

For me it’s more the stuff at work. Like the supervisors with the unit cameras. I’m sure they watch me through those, and then my shifts get changed, and everyone says, “No, it’s staffing shortages,” like that explains it. But it happens after they’ve been watching, like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up.

And then people talk around it like it’s normal, and I’m supposed to just accept that. But it feels like it’s meant for me, like the schedule change is because of me.
Do you ever feel like random things people do or say—like something on TV, a song playing, or even strangers talking—are sending you secret messages meant just for you?

Not like songs or TV talking to me, no. It’s more… like at work, the things people say are supposed to sound normal, like “staffing shortages,” but I don’t buy that.

The supervisors have those unit cameras, and I’m sure they’re watching me through them. Then my shifts get changed, and everyone acts like it’s just the schedule, like I’m supposed to just shrug and go home or come in at a different time. But it feels like it’s aimed at me, like they’re checking if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up.

I know that probably sounds like I’m taking it too personally, but when it keeps happening, it doesn’t feel random. It feels connected to me.

Do you feel that certain everyday events or actions by others—things that might seem normal or random to most people—are actually directly connected to you or have a special meaning for you that others don’t seem to notice?

Yeah, I do. I know people say it’s just normal work stuff, like staffing shortages or somebody called out, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.

Like the supervisors have those unit cameras, and I’m sure they watch me through them. Not just casually, like actually watching to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess something up. And then my shifts get changed after that, and everyone acts like it’s just scheduling.

It reminds me of when people say, “Oh, don’t take things personally,” but how am I not supposed to when it keeps happening around me? I worked hard to get that job, and I try to keep my head down, but then it’s like they’re moving me around for a reason. So yeah… it feels connected to me, even if other people don’t notice it.
Do you ever feel like things that are happening around you, like people’s actions or events, are directly controlled by someone or something to send you a specific message?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say “someone” like some big thing, but at work it feels like that.

Like the supervisors, with the unit cameras—they can see everything. And I’m sure they’re watching me through those, not just for normal stuff, but to see if I’m unsafe or if I’m going to mess up. Then my shifts get changed, and everybody says, “Oh, it’s staffing shortages,” like that’s supposed to make me feel stupid for noticing.

But it feels controlled, like it’s being done to send me the message that they’re watching me, that they don’t trust me there. I try to just do my job, you know, keep moving, help with the patients, clean up, all that… but then the schedule changes and it’s like, okay, why me again? It doesn’t feel random.

patient.answer:
I don’t think they’re, like, putting thoughts in my head exactly. Or hearing them word-for-word. It’s more… they already know what they’re looking for with me.

Like at work, with the cameras on the unit, I’m sure the supervisors are watching me to see if I’m unsafe. Then my shifts get changed, and everyone keeps saying it’s staffing shortages, but that doesn’t make sense to me because it happens after they’ve been watching. So maybe they don’t hear my thoughts, but they know enough. They act like they know what I’m going to do before I do it.
